questions.question_text: According to sommerfeld, the free electrons move with __________ potential.
questions.answer: The Sommerfeld model assumes electrons move in a constant potential within the metal bulk.

questions.question_text: The __________ is a geometrical construction to the Wigner-Seitz primitive cell in the K-space
questions.answer: The first Brillouin zone is the Wigner-Seitz primitive cell of the reciprocal (k-space) lattice.

questions.question_text: At zero Kelvin, F(E) takes the value __________ for any energy level above Fermi level
questions.answer: At T = 0K, the Fermi distribution is a step function; all states above Ef are empty (probability = 0).

questions.question_text: Identify the shape of the first Brillouin zone in Z-Dimensional lattice
questions.answer: For common 2D lattices (like the hexagonal/honeycomb lattice of graphene), the first Brillouin zone is hexagonal.

questions.question_text: In intrinsic semiconductor, the number of electrons equal to __________.
questions.answer: In an undoped semiconductor, electron-hole pairs are created thermally, ensuring n = p.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: When T = 0k, the Fermi energy (Ef) of n-type semiconductor is equal to
questions.answer: At 0K, the Fermi level in an n-type semiconductor lies exactly halfway between the donor level (Ed) and the bottom of the conduction band (Ec).
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: For a PN junction diode, the current in reverse bias may be __________.
questions.answer: In reverse bias, only the saturation current due to minority carriers flows, which is typically in the micro-to-nano ampere range.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: The expression for drift current density due to electrons is given by
questions.answer: Drift current density is J = nqeμeE (where qe is elementary charge).
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Which process of the Electron hole pair is responsible for emitting of light?
questions.answer: Radiative recombination of an electron and a hole results in the emission of a photon.

questions.question_text: Photon flow per unit area per second __________
questions.answer: Photon flux is defined as the number of photons passing through a unit area per unit time.

questions.question_text: __________ is the process where electron hole pairs created and recombined radiatively.
questions.answer: Photoluminescence involves photon absorption (creating EHP) followed by photon emission (radiative recombination).

questions.question_text: The Fermi's golden rule helps to identify the __________.
questions.answer: It is the fundamental equation for calculating transition probabilities per unit time.

questions.question_text: Two probe technique is suitable for measuring electrical resistivity of __________ samples.
questions.answer: Two-probe is used for high resistance samples where contact resistance is negligible compared to the sample resistance.

questions.question_text: __________ method used to measure the potential barrier of a P-N junction diode.
questions.answer: C-V measurements allow for the extraction of the built-in potential and doping profile.

questions.question_text: __________ is a method of determining quickly whether a semiconductor sample is n type (or) p type.
questions.answer: The Hot Probe method is a qualitative, quick check for carrier type.

questions.question_text: TCAD is a computer simulation technique that is widely used in the semiconductor industry. TCAD is an acronym for
questions.answer: TCAD stands for Technology Computer-Aided Design.

questions.question_text: The __________ density of states does not depend on energy.
questions.answer: In a 2D system (quantum well), the density of states is constant and independent of energy.

questions.question_text: An example for One – dimensional material is __________
questions.answer: Nanowires are 1D materials (confinement in two dimensions).

questions.question_text: In chemical vapour deposition, the precursors are introduced to the reaction chamber in the __________ state.
questions.answer: CVD precursors are always in a gaseous phase to undergo surface reactions.

questions.question_text: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) provides a __________ dimensional picture.
questions.answer: Standard TEM produces a two-dimensional projection of a three-dimensional specimen.
